dc_guide.text: This is the banqueting hall. That fireplace is Jacobean, carved for Sir Basil Brooke, who did the place up in the 1620s with English windows and Irish stone.

Before him, the O'Donnells, lords of Tír Chonaill. Red Hugh O'Donnell fought the English for nine years and his clan burned part of the castle rather than let them have it. The Irish way of saying 'no thank you'.

dc_visitor.text: I came for the castle and stayed for the spiral stairs. I have now gone round eleven times. I'm not sure which way is out.
